Like the full moon over the ocean of milk, he who is the nature of the primordial vibration spreads forth the sky of consciousness—unwavering, resonant with a vast sound, adorned with a garland of waves consisting of radiant points and curved rays;
may that trunk-like syllable OṂ, which manifests all at once, grant [fulfillment]. May the Vision of Action [bestow it].
May this Gaṇeśa, who has his abode in the teeth and whose birth was from Śakti, forcefully pacify all misfortune. || 1 ||
That which is here threefold— gross, subtle, and supreme— is the Word (Śabda), through the attainment of immersion in whose manifestation its own existence flashes forth from beyond,
having as its sole nature self-manifestation; that formless one, into whom the activity of reflective awareness has entered, is perceived as the course of worldly existence.
May that Lord remove the quality of darkness (tāmasī vṛtti) for the sake of illuminating the true path. || 2 ||

May this delightful hymn, appearing under a pretext, which is the moon born from the lineage of Kālidāsa, pacify for you the fever of the forest-fire of saṃsāra—[it being] drawn from the ocean of the moonlight of the sky of consciousness. (3)
If you desire to constantly behold Śiva with your inner eye, to realize His true nature within your lineage, and to attain the state of perfection, then devote your mind to this [Upāsanā]. 4.

Desiring the cave of the heart through the state of "I-ness," I approach Śiva—who possesses the form of vision and action yet is beyond the sphere of non-vision and non-action—who is ever-present and bestows equanimity; for the loss of friendship with Him indeed gives birth to suffering.

I take refuge in the auspicious Śiva and Śivā, who are the parents of the six paths; she who is the supreme speech uttered as "I am," and he whose embodied form is the self manifested by light, both of whom have arisen here together and are intent upon one another.

O Goddess, I clearly worship Mandara, the mountain that is Rudra himself—the churning rod for the ocean of the full moon's radiance, bound by the eye of Śakti, and the locus of the nectar-portion used for libation. || 7 ||
Among those people who existed in the past, who exist now, or who will exist in the future— each performing distinct actions— I am that one who,
with a singular and profound greatness, remains bowed within the cavity of the heart.

We pay homage to those great sages, headed by Patañjali, who fixed their minds upon the Lord, the eternal Self, the abode of the universe, who has attained the state of Puruṣa through the act of filling.
I ever take refuge in the mass of rays from the mouth of Khecarī, whose body is the power of the void (vyomaśakti),
wherein she desires to imitate the universe by means of the radiance of Śambhu’s son, Dakṣa.

I bow to you, Ambika, the sovereign mistress of all principles—the indivisible Lordly Reality (Īśvara-tattva) which is perceived by you through your throbbing, full existence that contains within it the expansion of the sixty-four parts. 11.
O Mother, he who is indeed Kilāsa is renowned as the Lord whose head is uplifted and agitated by noble beings; he upon whom you reside every day—that mountain is his very embodiment of being.

I bow to that Reality which is beyond conceptual construction and beyond the senses, which abandons the objective world as well as the outward-turned mind, and which dwells within the interval between existence and non-existence; O Eternal One, I am devoid of form before You.

O Mother, I worship that state of yours which, by its very nature, never abandons its sovereign freedom while remaining the emergence of non-duality; that state which is devoid of succession, known as Brahman, or as "Sat" (Being), or as "Cit" (Consciousness).

O Bhavānī, that which is designated as "place," "time," and "distinction"— and which follows the sequence based on individual, genus, and body— is merely the external manifestation of your own benefit.

O Mother! Of an object that has been brought into being, its body consists of *sattva* through the dawning of grace, and there is *tamas*, which is that which is prohibited; and *rajas* is both existent and non-existent, by virtue of its dual nature. (16)
O Śivā, that which is darkness (tamas) here is the body of the earth; that which is activity (sattva) here is distinct from fire.
The other, arising from their mixture, is passion (rajas). Thus, the triad of qualities (guṇatraya) is born from your sattva.
O Mother, you are the very essence of your husband, the Lord, whose nature is imperishable sovereignty;
knowledge, pure action, or their fruit are yours, as are the fruits of passionless perfection.

O Mother of Light, that which is perceived in the heart by means of knowledge is light; that which has spread forth in the sacrificial pavilion is the subtle element of air; and that which is heavy with the mark of smoke is fire—these three, however, are your body, consisting of the qualities of goodness (sattva), passion (rajas), and darkness (tamas).
O Caṇḍikā, for you indeed, upon beholding one being born within the side-glance of Rudra,
became like a pair of teachers of the paths of Sāṃkhya and Yoga, possessing both perfect understanding and meditative absorption.
O Śivā, by causing the world—which is already luminous—to be submerged [in darkness], you become the full moon;
yet, by making your own form appear otherwise [as if diminished], you are indeed perceived as the new moon (Kuhū).
O Kālī, you who abide in the sequence that transcends the interval between fullness and thinness,
you now desire to devour this present time, which is agitated by the divisions of sequential manifestation.

O Goddess, for what wise person would there not be liberation through that conceptual cognition—which consists of the knower, the known, and the means of knowledge—that arises from Your own creative power? For it is Your stainless nature that shines forth by means of it. 23.
Characterized by the reflective awareness of both the non-sequential and the sequential, you consist of both sequence and non-sequence;
having beheld the non-sequential Śiva who dwells in the center, this true lineage is your very face.

O Mother, destroy that state of atomicity residing within me—[the state] which, through Māyā capable of effecting the distinction between the knower and the known, proceeds sequentially through the limbs [of the body] and remains outside, longing for the senses. 25.

O Goddess! That karma which consists of various latent impressions (vāsanās) together with Māyā, whose nature is that of the individual soul (aṇu), is indeed dissolved by your mental states (vṛttis), just as darkness is dispelled by the rays of the sun. || 26 ||

Therefore, O Mother, by means of this secret and paradoxical practice (viparīta-caryā) which is invisible to the senses, Your all-consuming form is attained—a form in which all dualistic tendencies have been rendered into a state of equal flavor (samarasīkṛta). 27.

O Śivā, those powers characterized as the instruments that move within your conscious self in the sky, striving for the expansion of external objects— beyond them you indeed abide on the path leading upward.

O Sovereign, you who abide in seven ways as the locus of the qualities of consciousness, whose face is the peace of the void; you lead those who have taken refuge to no other than Śiva, transcending the state of duality and non-duality through the union of the two.

O Mother, what more need be said? This speech—Parā, which resides in the subject as the supreme inner self and whose form is pure awareness, and which manifests as the threefold states of existence—is itself speaking to you; how much more so, then, is Vaikharī?

O beloved of the Lord, beneath you, three forms of speech—consisting of sound (nāda), the point (bindu), and the written letter (lipi)—are uttered as sprays of reflective awareness directed upward within the abodes of withdrawal, maintenance, and emission. 31.

O Mother, show me that Śiva who dwells in the supreme sky upon the highest peak— He who moves through the void like fire, possessing the nature of vision and action, and whose light is like the moon and sun situated within it.

They consider the triad of speech beginning with *vaikharī* to be the object of knowledge and the means of knowledge; they remember the other [form] as the characteristic of the agent, whose body consists of emergence, persistence, and dissolution, and which possesses manifold divisions. (33)

O Mistress of the Kula! That divine form of yours, whose body is unseen as the universal form and which is the state of your supreme peace—whatever arising occurs therein, that emanation takes recourse in the fivefold movement.
O Ambikā, within that supreme power which vibrates in you like the waves of the ocean,
there exists the fivefold group of elements (*pañcatattva*), consisting of the subtle components of the *śiñjikā*, possessing various subtle forms.
O Goddess whose eyes are the three paths! Your face is the group of powers (*śakti-vṛnda*) consisting of the [three] *bhās*, according to the tradition;
it is the twelvefold sequence of stages, unfolded in this world by the four groups of three, beginning with the *pada*s. (As the tradition says. 36.

O Mother, the droplets of your [divine] play are indeed characterized by the three abodes—the Moon, the Sun, and Fire—which possess the eyes of the means of knowledge (pramāṇa), the objects of knowledge (prameya), and the knower (mātṛ); they are marked by the vowels divided according to the zodiac signs, the kings of the notes, and the ritual rules. 37.

O Śivātmikā, from Your feet arises the vowel, which is the expressive word (*vācaka*) consisting of the expansion of consciousness regarding the object; it is non-dual, yet its body is the manifestation of vision and reflective awareness (*vimarśa*), and it is the support for that which is otherwise difficult to transcend. (38)
O Mother! The articulated sound (*vaikharī*), produced by the effort of manifesting the breath, resounds when struck;
however, this mental sound (*mānasī*) is unstruck (*anāhata*), and the latter is perceived as being perfumed by You. (39)

O Auspicious Śivā, all the digits of the moon—excluding the sixth, those possessing the splendor of the letter *ma*, and those devoid of the nasal bindu—are indeed the wombs that hold the seed-syllables (*bīja*) and their corresponding vowels. 40.

O Mother, your power, which is composed of action and possesses the characteristics of a well-formed mother— the alphabet (mātṛkā) differentiated by the various methods of seed-syllables and matrices— is victorious as the supreme form of the Lord.

The Bindu, consisting of the imperishable syllable and composed of action, which controls that which is characterized by the intellect—Nāda is its desired form and its cause; O Supreme One! You are she whose nature consists of this triad. 42.

O Sovereign Lady, the first wave of Your ocean of consciousness—which is Śiva, tranquil and free of ripples—is exertion; prior to the assumption of the state of unawakened consciousness, O Goddess, Your body is the sky, which is of great exaltation.

This very cognition, expanded and having attained the state of moving through the sky, has followed the wheel of the senses in every direction; O Bhava, you yourself have reached the station of its range within the sense-objects. 44.
O Mother! That quartet beginning with Khecarī, which possesses parts, is Your external body;
that which devours the distinction between duality and non-duality is partless, not external, and beyond the reach of words.
O Mother! Your body, consisting of the fivefold activity, has emerged as the Śakti that bestows the splendor of the Kula;
having united with Śiva from the Akula, you therefore find rest there once again. (46)
O Mother! By reason, your fivefold function is observed as the function of the qualities of the five elements;
that which is produced by the function of the substratum (dharmin) is named "Siddhi," while that which is produced by the function of the attribute (dharma) is named "Śakti" for you.
He who meditates upon your form, beginning with the five Siddhas starting from Brahmā and the five Śaktis starting from Bhāratī, along with Unmanī, is victorious on the path of the Siddhas. (48)
Whatever object, consisting of the nature of both the substrate and its attributes, You illuminate, that is created within the Lord;
whatever illumination exists here, it is brought forth by You and assumes the state of creation through the forms of those various shapes.
For you, who are devoted to consciousness, there is no state of consciousness in itself apart from the consciousness of objects;
if you remain even without the circle of objects at the limit of creation, how can there be any state of consciousness?

If latent impressions (*vāsanā*) do not constitute the locus of diversity, and you alone are their progenitor here, then you—whose womb bears the world characterized by power (*śakti*), and who brings forth all things mental and sensory—are the Mother. (51)

O Mother, this entire world is illumined by you at all times: internally, upon the mirror of the intellect, through your form as consciousness; and externally, in the present moment, through your form as the senses.

O Mother! As long as there is a state of tranquility for a person who abides within all states of being—this is the seventh [state]—so long does the state of being permeated by eternal *vimarśa* exist, wherein the distinction from non-dual *vimarśa* has vanished. (53)
O Mother, that which is called inert by those who perceive through dualistic qualities, yet which is gradually manifested as it dispels them—
that which is the very form of consciousness, devoid of external form, and which shines forth by itself all at once— you alone are that.
O Mother! That dullness which belongs to the world by its very nature appears as duality from the highest [Brahman] downwards;
but you are known as the adversary of that dullness, for you shine once and for all within the entire circle of objects.

O Mother, you who are determined as "I" through the absence of name and form—this entire universe is that very you! You do not possess the state of being an object of illumination, for you are the light of the Self, the attribute of the Sovereign Lord.

The visionary of existence, relying on the "jewel of emptiness" in the Lord—a person devoid of traditional scripture and beyond definition—maintains that this world exists; yet it is not so, for it does not abide on the upward path of the dissolution of consciousness.
Devoted to peace, you have attained that independent state which is the sole abode of the world consisting of mere potentiality;
for the entire universe has been submerged by you within that radiance, like the world being purified by a stainless fire.
This multitude of objects, which exists as a state of pervasion through the manifestation of subjects consisting of perfected powers, attains its full luminosity;
you cause it to expand toward your own perceiver in your presence.

That which is the state of being a seer in the manifestation of the world, that which is the state of being a knower in the process of ascertainment, and even the state of being a grasper in the apprehension of what has been ascertained—he knows all this, O Lord, when nourished by Your activity. (60)

Established within the mandala of existent and non-existent objects, possessing an intellect whose body is the senses and who consists of smiles, he who is thirteenfold is that very sovereignty; I am that duality, a portion of you.
This Supreme Person, whose form is bliss characterized by the enjoyment of various objects,
shines within the ether of consciousness as the dissolution of the universe within you, O Śivā, through the act of offering.
O Śivā, that city which, having attained a subtle state pertaining to the Liṅga, manifests eightfold within you—
may the latent impressions of those whose mental fluctuations are perfected through the recitation of that [city] reside in the womb of the bound soul (paśu).

O Śivā, between these two— the body of the manifest world and the body of conventional reality— which occupy the positions of the eater and the eaten, I have been established by you as the intellect, mind, senses, and physical form.

O auspicious one, because of your sovereignty and because you delight the subjects, I am known by the name "Rāja" (King) among the functions of awakening and action; these six distinct motivators have been placed by you in the state of being my sons.
The solar breath (*prāṇasūrya*), characterized by the upward-flowing *bindu*, consists here of six consciousness-parts (*ciddviṣaṭkala*).
You are that possessor of the body of those parts within the lineage of Gurus; you are the body of light, the circle of perfected ones (*siddhamaṇḍala*).
That apāna-soma, whose characteristic is downward-flowing and which here constitutes the body of experience,
has been fashioned by you into sixteen digits (kalās) within the lineage of gurus, having the wheels of bliss (ānandacakra) as their bodies.
O Caṇḍī, as long as the digits of the lords of day and night extend their rising,
even so long does the rise of day and night occur through you, whose form is both manifest and hidden.

O Goddess, that state which reaches the plane of *sāmarasya* (perfect equilibrium) through the blending of the two aspects (*kalā*) is indeed Your form here, situated within the object of knowledge (*vedya*), the means of knowledge (*vedaka*), and the *bindu* and *nāda*. 69.
O Śivā, you have assumed a state in which the orbs of the sun and moon are licked by the fire of universal dissolution;
existing as the seventeenfold breath within the abode of life, your form has taken refuge in the lineage of the Gurus.
The powers that effect the desired [results] were withdrawn by You from the abodes of dissolution, maintenance, and emanation;
they have been extended from the state of deep sleep onwards toward the three stations, reaching the level of the fourth consciousness.

O Mother Ambikā, that fourth state of yours, which is sought by the great ones as being beyond description, is the family characterized by the object of knowledge, the knower, and the act of knowing, wherein it finally comes to rest.
Through the worship of You with the various offerings of *cāru*, *rāva*, and *caru*, accompanied by the *mudrā*, Your lineage—
possessing a manifest form— attains its state through that very sequence.

O Maṅgalā, you are she who shines as the supreme [power] within the fourfold speech and the circle of forms; you are worshipped in the form of the letters of sound and the point (nāda-bindu-lipi), abiding in the wheel of the multitude of light and bliss.
O Mother, when the primordial form of the expansion of consciousness, having taken its seat therein, attains a yellow hue,
the person born from the wheel of power (śakticakra), by worshipping that imperishable Śiva, is liberated.

O Mother! When Śiva, in a state of equanimity, is awakened by you through your form as Śakti, that powerful Vīrya (vital energy) which then shines forth—this indeed is the great Pīṭha arisen from you.

That inexhaustible power of vibration within Śiva, whose manifest body is established in the five elements beginning with earth, becomes the supreme *vīrya*; you, who consist of that very essence, are the mother of the *pīṭhas* and *cakras*.

O Mother, you abide everywhere at all times as the single essence of the multitude of sacred seats and wheels; you are perceived by the virtuous, whose very selves are characterized by incessant exertion, as one whose arising is unrestrained.

This group of syllables, which attains heroism through various movements, reaches that final Lord who possesses three abodes; the power of the phonemes is the state of the plane of consciousness (citkalā).
O Śiva, that [power] which has the form of fire, sun, and moon, and which spreads through the unstruck sky of the subtle energies (kalās)—
as long as she is worshipped from the sacred seats (pīṭhas) onwards, she, being identical with that [reality], becomes manifest.

O Umā! Your seat is the eightfold mantra (the Gāyatrī), which consists of the manifestation of the state of abiding in solitude; it is eternal, unrestrained in its arising, expanded, and illuminated by the side-glances of You. 81.
O Karavīra, you who possess a constant aversion to light, who consume everything, and who are difficult even for the gods to behold, yet serve as the abode of the virtuous—
you are worshipped by us, though you dwell in cremation grounds, take delight in the hearts of heroes, and have your vitality diminished.

O Lord, I rejoice in Your self-awareness (*vimarśa*), which is intensely fierce in its play of universal dissolution, eternally arisen in the supportless void, and shining forth as the unconditioned Protector of the Field (*kṣetrapāla*). 83.

O Mother, this lineage of your gurus, beginning with Khecarī and ending with Śākinī, as well as this entire cycle of emanation and the inexplicable power [of manifestation], are all your own emergence. (84)
O Mother! That which shines forth as this duality exists here eternally through state-of-equipoise (sāmarasya); this is Your own abode, where joy perpetually unfolds, standing before me. 85.
The mind, which consists of five vehicles and is a devourer of the objects of enjoyment, the enjoyer, and desire, is called darkness;
where those [five] reach their stationless state, there is that certain perpetual festival of sacrifice.
Empowered by the hearts of those filled with sattva, rajas, and the other qualities, you carry all the worlds;
arising eternally in fivefold ways, you are served by the perfected ones like the river of the Siddhas.
Preceded by the wise one in his celestial vehicle, this fivefold expansion of yours has now pervaded the world,
its form shining upon the path of the sky through the opening of your great mouth.
O Śivā, following your initial vibration, you have arisen upon the path that is without abode through the qualities;
you dwell in the abode of the void by your own will, and having first established your voice, you manifest yourself.
O Mother, you who were formerly that very Khecarī, overflowing with the established wonder of the "Cic" [the Point],
now manifest as this desire displayed through the gathering of forms by means of your spontaneously flowing splendor.

O Goddess, you alone are she who moves upon the earth (*bhūcarī*), clearly ascending through the exertion toward manifold objects; ever facing the grasping of touch, you do not abandon the freedom born of your own nature.

O Goddess, that very same power of vision, which contracts within the inner self and spreads the entire universe as food within the belly, moves through the quarters by means of its face of consumption; she is intent upon the chewing of the aesthetic essence (rasa). 92.
Having swiftly attained your own nature, which is without abode, from the very mouth of the realized mind,
you have become manifest as Gandhahāriṇī, whose external expansion is brought about by the state of Raudra.

O Śivā, your digit, which ascends the limbs of the form of Brahmā and constitutes the essence of the five-fold vehicle, shines eternally within the assembly of Siddhas, its arising fashioned through the state of aesthetic identity (sāmarasya). 94.
The power of Rudra, Kālakarṣiṇī, who delineates the higher and lower planes through the sun, moon, fire, Kuṇḍalinī, the bindu, and the sūtra, indicates here your fivefold activity.

O Śivā, I bow to you here, who are fashioned from the five digits (kalās)—the syllable *ghoṣa* (gh), the *vāḍava-śikhā* (au), that which follows it (*u*), the pair consisting of *bindu* and *nāda* (m), and the *pada* (om)—together with the grace of *pra* (pra). Thus, you are the very *Om*. 96.

O Goddess, you have revealed to me that which consists of pure consciousness: the five stages supported by the seeds of the Moon, the Trident, the Bull, the Mother, and Time; and the arising of the Pole Star (Dhruva) established through elision and euphonic combination. 97.

O Mother, that which is the state of fever and the like, that crest of fire with its honey and venomous serpents, and that night which encompasses the creation established in sweetness—even the *paṅkti* meter imitates Your state. 98.
O Mother, that sky which throbs, that wind which is presided over and sustained by you in the form of creation,
that crest of flame, that water, and even that row of sacrificial fires— by these, you are likewise of such a nature.
O Śivā, you move upon the earth by means of the staff (daṇḍa), and that other tetrad proceeds from the skull (muṇḍa);
when the waves of the conceptualization of the enjoyed and the enjoyer are exhausted, you rise in the essence of aesthetic flavor (sāmarasya-rasa).

O Goddess, that sound which is unstruck, sustained by the upward path, and situated in the sky at the root of the three triangles— therein you flow in five ways through successive stages, positioned between the sides of space and fire.

O Mother, you who consist of the five groups and whose body is the fivefold bed, you shine like a letter, O Goddess, having emerged with the fivefold functions produced by the state of aesthetic relish (sāmarasya). 102.
O Mother, you are called the Great Void because you are eternally arisen here in this sky;
emitting divine and unfailing [power], you indeed abandon [all] touch, for your form is beautiful.

O Śivā, that very same faultless consciousness, having reached the supreme state of the ether by its own nature, shines forth brilliantly upon attaining supreme vibration; O Sky-farer, the sky-dwellers bow down before you.
O Śivā, you are clearly the manifestation of the non-sequential, from whom the emergence of the two worlds is emitted;
when you move about having taken recourse [to a body], you then become known by the name Bhūcarī.

O Ambikā, your own body, characterized by the power of vibration, becomes composed of each respective object in an instant; yet if that very power remains within your own state, you then withdraw it and become the one who moves through the quarters.

With her face turned inward, she swallows her own threefold sequence— which, through the destruction of duality, has been projected into a state of uniformity— if indeed she is that very [Power] who extends to the end of the great void.
O Goddess, if any one among the five modes of being— which are identical with You— vibrates by itself,
then at that very moment all of them, having ascended to a state of aesthetic oneness (sāmarasya), shine forth eternally and instantaneously.
O Mother, by you who desire the sky, the Sky-farer (Khecarī) has been expanded through the state of being without abode;
and by her, the Quarter-farer (Dikcarī), who has clearly established her own majesty within the creation of Sound (nāda), has been presided over.

O Mother! You, whose body is the sound of the sixteen rays [of the vowels] as desired, who abide upon the ground of the Bindu and possess the manifest glory of the wheel of bliss, are the one who moves upon the earth (Bhūcarī). 110.
O Mother, you are the Dikcarī, the radiance of the Bindu; having expanded here, you have emerged externally.
Swallowing the five-fold objects of experience, you lead Bhūcarī to a state of non-differentiation.
Having ascended the wheel of forms— which has the body of fire with ten and a half digits and seven flames, and which devours everything— you, O Dikcarī, enter the supreme non-dual Speech.

O Mother, having dispelled the intoxication of the mind through your own unfolding, you have reached your own sky which is beyond the realm of the earth; grasping the supreme state of consciousness, O Auspicious One, you are the transcendent one whose mental afflictions have been shaken off.
You, whose nature is the expansion of the foremost of the unstruck sounds (*asvara*), who strive for the complete union with the wheel of the universe,
and who transcend the conceptualization of meditative cultivation and other such mental constructs— you are worshipped upon the preeminent seat of the Five-Faced One.

Resplendent upon the seats of Bindu, Nāda, and Śaśi, with a form that is the dark embodiment of the King of Flames, you are Maṅgalā, whose nature is the supreme ether called Asvara, transcending the threefold speech. 115.
O Śivā, the consciousness residing in the sixteen abodes perpetually expands her own power;
she, whose station is without abode, constantly radiates forth a multitude of rays of knowledge.
O female skeleton, these hands of yours which are both inside and outside, and this very body of yours that remains unbroken—
by means of these two forms, you lead us, O skeletal woman, into the sky of consciousness beyond.

Since the mandala of reality, which has the earth as its surface and is the limit of primordial nature, is the abode of limited planets, you are Krodhanī; it is out of a desire to dissolve that very [reality] that your mantra-form manifests here.

O Goddess, you bring forth that supreme vigor— the body known as the aggregate of causes and instruments, consisting of the qualities emanating from the three powers, and filled with the intense flavor of mantra— with the desire to withdraw it.

O Bhairavī, you who hold even the six knots within yourself, you are the state of the sky of consciousness free from veils; bearing the grand display of duality through the form of vibration, you are the one who pierces through the universe. 120.

O Mother, you who possess a mass of rays intent on withdrawing the latent impressions of the seeds uttered from the eight cities, having merely licked and then split open my mouth, [protect me] with your ever-licking tongue.

O Goddess, you who are intent upon dissolving the expansion of the final manifest sound (*vaikhari*) starting from the supreme (*parā*), you become the sky-faring goddess (*khecarī*) who expands consciousness and dwells in the abode of Śambhu, which is without veil. 122.
O Mother, devouring the abodes of fire, sun, and moon, you—Kuṇḍalinī—are leaping up like lightning;
O Śāmbhavī, you have become the Sky-farer (Khecarī) by entering the Bindu through the middle path.
Sealed by the maṇḍala of reality created by yourself, you yawn within your own belly, eternally arisen;
O Śivā, entering the fivefold divisions within the circle of the Vṛnda, you bestow the glory born of yoga.
O Mother, through those vowels of yours which are differentiated and devoid of the neuter ones, there arises here a union;
and through the consonants beginning with *ka* and *ha*, joined with the two powers of mantra, the Great One (*Mahāntika*) emerges.
The Binducakra, Śaśi, Kuṇḍalī, Śikhā, and Mūrti—these four kinds [of energies] have entered the sky;
here, the Power (Śakti) has effected the piercing of Śambhu, and the sixty-four Parās have entered the sky.
The sixty-four rays that emerged from your own body, beginning with the letter *ā* and ending with *ha*,
have been established by you within the belly of Khecarī in Maṅgala through supreme non-duality.
Ambikā shines forth through the rays of knowledge as Raudrī, through the rays of mantra as Vāmā, and through the rays of yoga as Jyeṣṭhā; thus she manifests from the rays of power (śakti). 128.
O Goddess, the vowel shines within the rays of Śambhu, inseparable from the four kalās;
you too abide therein, distinguishing the phonemes, since you bear preeminence within Maṅgalā.
Always rising at once and everywhere destroying the distinctions of conceptual construction,
you have thus expanded your own rays of light— the marks of your nature— through this single body into the vast expanse.

O Mother, that activity which consists of exertion, expansion, and relishing—the states of waking and so forth—and even that fourth state which is their dissolution, you manifest as the body of light throughout all this. 131.

O Mother Ambikā, that primordial awareness which shines forth, free from conceptual construction and mounted upon the circle of the senses, is here the manifestation facing toward it; that is your body, O Knower, which sustains all objects.

That reflective awareness which arises within, unimpaired, as the established manifestation of "this is such-and-such," is the mantra residing in your circle of Vṛnda; for by means of it, your ritual action becomes effective.

O Mother! Your yoga, which merges the entire universe, arises from the fullness of pure bliss shining forth through the friction between the enjoyed and the enjoyer; it sets all the functions of the senses in motion. 134.
Having ascended by the light of consciousness to the state of non-conceptuality, which is mere cognition free from latent impressions,
you indeed abide as the Power within the Lord, bringing about eternal emergence through the state of aesthetic equilibrium (sāmarasya).

O Mother, you who have entered the great void of the sky—which is indeed empty, the seed of vibration, and without abode—by means of that consciousness (citta) you dissolve instantly; through you, whose body is like the rays of Śambhu, he becomes manifest here.
O Mother, you are called Jñāna, the long-tongued serpent gliding upon the ocean of consciousness filled with tranquility;
you are the hundred-headed one whose form is the destruction of the sequence of that [consciousness] and its dependent [objects], abiding in the upper sphere.

O Śivā, having ascended the multitude of objective phenomena which consist of the essence of the fluid of consciousness that is Śiva in the state of becoming, you expand forth from Śambhu, manifesting as ether, air, fire, water, and earth. 138.

O Mother! Your splendors, which consist of the essence of wealth being whirled by the fire of your expansive awareness, possess the forms of the seeds of the five divine families and bestow the sky of consciousness that is Śiva. 139.

This tree of the sequence of the five [kulas], whose fruit is the realization of Śiva free from conceptual construction, unfolds with its body as the five wheels; yet within the rays of your splendor, O Śivā, its own majesty is cast aside.
O Mother! This seed-syllable, which is the unfolding sequence of the fivefold deities manifested from you, is the bestower of perfection;
this unobstructed radiance, which expands here, resides within the inner wheel.
In the abode of Śambhu you are Ambareśvarī; thereafter, in the abode of Śakti, you are Khecarī;
then, in the abode of Yoga, you are Bhūcarī; and thereafter, in the abode of Mantra, you are Dikcarī.
O Sovereign of all, you flash forth from the fifth [state] by suddenly leaping into the sequence;
yet, O Goddess of the abode of gnosis, no sequence exists for you in that supportless state.
O Śivā, from the point of primordial knowledge onwards, you who are here the body of the sky of supreme consciousness shine forth as the fifth [state],
pregnant with the power consisting of the five vehicles, devouring the banner of manifestation.
O Mother, you are the essence of the uninterrupted sky of consciousness; by your shore, O ocean of compassion, you are measured.
Within you, the rivers of consciousness, being without fixed abode, instantly attain fullness.

O Śivā, this wheel of yours, whose majesty consists of fivefold emanations, has been brought here within the range of perception; it never at any time falls away from your foot, which is consciousness alone, beyond all description, and the devourer of the universe. 146.
That abode which exists together with the mudrā, that consciousness which rests in the sanctuary of the soul,
and that creative power (kalā) endowed with atomic manifestation— all that, O Mother, is contained within your circle of the multitude (vṛndacakragam).

This sound (*nāda*) of yours, which is the seed of the flashing forth of the unmanifest, which is foremost, devoid of form, and free from sequential order, is the unique Lord of consciousness—the reflective awareness that is the teacher of the universe. (148)

O Mother, this consciousness—which pierces the five knots and is indicated by the functioning of the five-pointed syllables—is that formless body of yours in the supreme abode, consisting of the five wombs (yonipañcaka). 149.
O Mother, you have sealed with your expansive manifestations born from the five groups consisting of touch and color;
you are the world itself, pervading everywhere through the arrangement of distinct individualities, united with the abode of manifestation.

O Mother, that which is inherently without succession, yet consists of the five sources (yonis) composed of succession from the very beginning, manifests as having succession—characterized by emanation—by virtue of its dependence upon You, even while remaining essentially free of succession. 151.
In this world, your source alone is considered by the wise to be the non-sequential embodiment of Yoga;
that which is your manifestation here is the great source, superior even to that.
O Mother, since your conduct has been maintained as superior to that of Śaṅkhayoni,
and since you possess the four castes, even the lotus-born Brahmā— who delights in the manifestation of the body of Time— is surpassed by your blossoming splendor.
O Kālī, you abide in the manner of a waveless ocean within your own abode that devours all duality;
here, you are of divine origin and identical with your own essential nature, while your supreme manifestation is devoid of inherent being.

Having assumed bodies through the perfection of perceiving the universal form consisting of their own essential nature, those five sources, who maintain the circle of creation, ascended to the tangible form. 155.

O Great Bird, O Mother, the circle of perfected masters—their nature that of the subject flashing forth as the non-dual unfolding of the four quarters at the threshold of awakening—is the state of non-duality beyond duality, attained by you instantly. 156.

O Sāmba, your renown here is that of the incarnation of exalted majesty who is the guardian of the cosmic order— the sequence of the world which, from its manifestation onward, resides within the fourfold vowels at the heart of the sacrificial pit (Kuṇḍa).
O Mother, he who takes refuge here in the Swan— the imperishable sky-goer whose form is vibration and who is devoid of touch—
and who, as the Lord, dwells in the abode that consumes the three paths, attains the state of the Lord of Birds.

O Mother, that first impulse of intuition—which is non-dual and intent upon the wondrous creation of the universe—assumes the state of a tortoise when placed upon Your path, following the manner of a tortoise's movement. 159.
O Umā, this supreme rising of mine, which bears the form of a ram according to my will, approaches your abode;
though its greatness is eternally transcendent, it enters into a state of stability within you as if swallowing all things.

"O Śivā, he commands you thus: 'O consciousness, dwell in my state which is free of support, where the conceptualizations of external objects and the attainment of established categories have been liberated. Thus, O auspicious one, he is unrestrained for you. (161)

O Umā, the fish of consciousness, having entered the mouth of intense reflective awareness (*vimarśa*), has turned back from all sequential movement within the ocean of the supreme non-dual manifestation that is free of waves; it swallows the entire universe into its belly.
O Mother, this process of Your manifestation is of infinite majesty and formless;
therein the multitude of powers, concentrated as they expand from the power residing within You, unfolds.
O Mother, your Krama, which begins with *kṣānta* and proceeds through the wheel of the senses (*akṣacakra*), performs the investigation that dispels the intellect;
arisen as the "Wheel of Fragments" (*khaṇḍacakra*), it consists of eleven stages and is the sequence of withdrawal (*saṃhṛtikrama*) here.

Free from the instruction of grasping at certainties, transcending both logic and illogic, and beyond sequence—this supreme, intense expansion of the Khandacakra within Śiva has ascended to the celestial abode arising on the true path. 165.

O Mother, your lineage-succession (*anvayakrama*) is one that conceals the manifestation of both the manifest and its other (the unmanifest), destroys the sequence of the external world, and unfolds from the emergence of the supreme reality beyond the base; it is thus fully perfected. 166.
O Mother, the pair of sounds (nāda-yugma), which is intent on resting here within the agitation of the grasped object and its grasper,
desires to devour this [sound] numbering eleven (rudra-saṃkhyam) in your [throat], O Ambikā.

O Kālakarṣiṇī, your radiance shines forth for the destruction of that which is established in the ten senses, which is excessively uprooted, and which is overwhelmed by the distinction between self and insentient matter. 168.

O Umā, he who, filled with the wonder of consciousness, swallows here his own respective objects by means of the collection of the wheels of the senses numbering twelve like the sun— he, having attained that state, shines forth as the inner self.

O Goddess, having been instantly led to that state, those whose mental continuums have reached Your abode of the Fourth (turya) become established in the essence of the waveless supreme ether; thus, their radiant energies attain a state of perfect aesthetic fusion (sāmarasya).

O Mother, your wheel of the radiance of objective reality stands outside, manifesting through its total dedication to that [inner wheel], moving within the wheel of the self-luminous sounds of your own nature, which are devoid of the divisions of the initial creation. 171.
O Lord, if the rays of light from you— which rest upon the supreme sky of non-conceptuality and have abandoned all other states—
were indeed expanded, they would bring about a state of total fullness and a sense of wonder regarding the external world in this universe.
O Mother, that supreme wave of your flickering and surging activity, which moves like lightning,
has from its very birth been once and for all abandoned by the three modes of existence, without any conceptual construction.
O Mother, that differentiation—the sequential process occurring within its own path during emanation—is distinct from that [emanation];
it is stainless, yet accumulated by the four waves consisting primarily of the exertion of the sequence of bodies. 174.

O Mother, one alone is Your unobscured splendor—the tumultuous surge of the twelve-fold sequence of consciousness—which arises as the Goddess Sṛṣṭikālī at Your mouth; it is manifest, boundless, and without support. (175)

O Goddess, by the power of that which was produced from Hara, this mass of your luster—possessing a body difficult to behold and a lofty abode—is twofold in its sequence and non-sequence, as ordained by its own nature. (176)

O Goddess, you are Bhairava, whose state is your own essential nature as the fourfold self; you are beyond the mind and the state of trans-mind (*manonmanī*), possessing a body that is the unity of the twelve [suns], wherein sequence and non-sequence are one. You are their very foundation. 177.
Because it attains the forms of Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Hara, that fourth abode of yours is the void;
O Śivā, your sequential utterance is proclaimed as moving within the wheel of dissolution.
O Mother, that which is placed within the Bindu, residing in the three abodes, distinguished by that [Bindu], and ascends upward—
the *oṃ* which is the dissolution of differentiation— that alone is the perception of the Supreme Reality.

O Lord, the rays of the fire of Time, which extend from the world of Sattvaja up to the limit of the Śruta-kalā, have been spread out by you for the devouring of the universe; it is because of this dissolution that men cast off their state of atomicity.

O Caṇḍikā, the portions [of time] that arise from the expansion of the syllables of the mantra, as well as the circle of principles (tattva-maṇḍala) and whatever worlds exist therein— all of that is entirely contained within her state of persistence.

O Mother, you are eternally praised by yogis who have resorted to the method of being free from obstacles and have accomplished non-dual contemplation through you, while having established within themselves the pavilions of the six paths.
O Śivā, immerse this world— which from its very root rests upon the Fire and finds its end at the Dvādaśānta— into Your own abode, the plane of consciousness,
as You abide in the expansion of that [Fire] through the movement of the vital breath.
For those who possess the reasoning that is free from obscuration, that supreme space shines forth,
wherein even the latent impression (vāsanā) does not reside in the differentiation of the world, since it has devoured the objects of knowledge, the means of cognition, and the cognizer.
The withdrawal of one's conduct is indeed manifested toward a mother, yet there is certainly no diminution of affection;
both of these qualities are gathered in Your abode, O Fierce One—this very ferocity of Yours! 185.
O Mother, your powers, which are the abode of the machine of the elements, reside within the group of the imperishable senses;
for they worship your state with the nectar-liquor of sense-objects and the flowers of their respective functions. 186.

Having dissolved the six elements, beginning with the field of perception (gocara) and ending with emptiness (śūnya), into Your abode— which is self-luminous— the supreme powers, overflowing with joy, manifest their pride within the Lord.
O Mother! In your sky, known as the fire of the Mothers, the rays of the twelve-fold sun suddenly enter and consume the universe—the world reflected in the mirror of consciousness. 188.
O Sovereign Lady, this body, which resembles a reflection in a flawless mirror, has attained pervasiveness within Your space; it cannot logically exist outside of that reflection.
If it were to manifest that "the external exists," then that [existence] would indeed be permeated by such a manifestation.
O Mother, a means of knowledge (*pramāṇa*) certainly establishes manifestation; however, that which is devoid of a means of knowledge does not bring it to awareness. (190)
"This is such-and-such," and "the fruit is indeed thus"—such is the internal reflection;
it is unimpeded like the word *upadhāna*. That triad of folds resides within you as the object of action.
Even though it exists within as an illusion, the world appears as if external in its present state;
yet, O Mother, through your wisdom in the form of active consciousness, the pair of past and future remains just as it was before.
You abide in the cave [of the heart] with a form that illumines, concealing all states of being;
and he who is your Lord dwells in the cave, and the entire cycle of living beings is his city.
O Mother, it has been said that the mind imitates this external reflection produced by illusion;
yet both of these—the mother and her reflection—are mirrored within your own body, wherein this duality abides.

O maiden, the clarity of reflection is manifest in water, fire, mirrors, and other such transparent objects; yet, because it was consecrated along with its retinue, your own reflected image was not perceived by them. 195.

That object which flashes forth in memory, and that which appears in dreams and mental projections— since these are observed here to be devoid of a physical prototype, the world, though submerged in you, has arisen from you as its reflection.
If this divine word— that "what is seen in a dream is unreal"— is here established as authoritative,
then even a mental construction is not false, since its fruit, which arises from the meditation on Garuḍa and the like, resides in Śiva.

O Mother! If this manifestation, consisting of the conceptualization "it is thus," reaches fullness, then the subsequent reflective awareness "it is indeed so" does not remain within [the initial state] and thus becomes fit for complete sublation. (198)
O Goddess, if that [power] is held by a person on water or land, or likewise in fire, the sun, or the moon;
or in the wind or in the sky—then indeed that person assumes its form and performs its actions. (199)
If conceptualization is said to be false, by what cause does meditative concentration bear fruit?
O Goddess, since you are the life-force of the cognition that synthesizes all things, why are you not worshipped by anyone? 200.
They did not go there; by his own reasoning, Viṣṇu showed his son to them, saying:
"O Father, O Mother, this son of yours has been consumed by Śaṅkara; indeed, this is your external course."
Hari will assume the form of Hayānana, and he who is known as Gopa has gone outside the city;
if these two do not yield external results for those who worship them, O Mother, then that which is beyond the past cannot be real.

O Mother, in that supreme syllable where the Ṛgveda and all the deities reside—if one does not realize that, then the fruit of the Ṛgveda for those who know it is not attained; such indeed is the clear scriptural testimony. (203)
Fire, the sun, the moon, lightning, heat, the firefly, the celestial wanderers, and others—
whatever luminous things flash within the heart, they indeed exist as being contained within that very sky.
Whatever appears with its specific place and time, exactly as it was experienced by that distinct subject, all of that is perceived by her in memory; for a moment, she beholds my own memory.
If that experience [of the Lord] were not to perish, it would be remembered as "that";
for familiarity resides in both experience and memory. Upon the destruction of that [experience], there is only experience, not memory. (206)

Recollection (*saṃsmṛti*) is the cognition of a similar object; the object of recollection is indeed that which has been previously seen, distinct from [the present] perception. When the vision of Śiva—which consists in the manifestation of the object—is brought forth, this very manifestation is what is called "recollection. (207)

O Mother, this world—characterized by the seer, the seen, and the act of seeing—was withdrawn into you prior to its recollection; yet at the emergence of that memory, it unfolds again, and at its dissolution, it closes by your will alone. (208)
O Mother, that memory which is the very life of the knower here, and that vision which manifests his effort— even these two, when concealed by you, together once again assume a state of deformity.
O Mother Ambikā, vision creates this universe here, and your memory stabilizes it once more;
yet you yourself, established upon those two, abide as the unattached darkness of yoga.
O Mother, you bear the form characterized by creation, preservation, and dissolution, yet you possess the nature of the *bindu*;
being of a state distinct from those, you are said to be the embodiment of consciousness and, once again, formless.

O Goddess, your self-reflection (vimarśa), which is the expansion of the sun through the blending of fire and moon, has firmly established me—consisting of both the enjoyed and the enjoyer and abiding in self-awareness—within the womb of consciousness in this state. 212.
O Mother, this world, which has been cultivated as the form of vision, becomes the form of stability through the rays that constitute its making;
yet, by means of this very self, it would become indefinable through the logic of having no abode, and would then undergo dissolution.

The seed-syllable *bindu*, which consists of half the form of the *nyāsa* (arrangement) gathered from the piercing of the senses, the roots, the animals, and the disjunctions, shines forth as such through absorption into Your state where all conceptualization has withered; why then [is it called] a *mudrā*? 214.

O Mother, that supreme Consciousness which shines at once in all ways and in every state throughout the entire universe—that very Reality, whose manifestation is the unfolding of the world through secret speech, attains the nature of Mantra. 215.
O Śivā, spreading within your womb a fierce fire whose flames extend only as far as your eyes,
you swallow the digits of the sun— the very body of Time— and at your own rising, you manifest the expansion of your power.

May that emptiness of the existence and non-existence of objects, wherein liberation triumphs and where [the mind] finds rest—devoid of the mother, her instruments, and their objects—be my dissolution at all times. 217.
O Mother, He extends time through calculation, yet its apprehension occurs suddenly within the three worlds;
that time is indeed non-sequential for the Lord, and You, O Goddess, are its very embodiment.
In the sky enveloped by external clouds, you bear a radiance that dispels darkness in the form of a smile;
yet in the sky of consciousness enveloped by Māyā, you draw that [darkness] away, for you are perceived by the supreme ones.
O Caṇḍī! You are the excellent ground of Śiva, who is Kālī and Kāla, and you devour the twelve suns of the self; those who have mastered conceptualization know you to be exactly as you are.
O Mother, that great manifestation which is observed as existence arising from the threefold family—that ocean of all conceptual constructs therein, you are; you are its wave, ever eager for action.

O Mother, you are that auspicious wave of the ocean of Śiva, intent upon the grasping that reveals the tossing of this entire universe—which, though consisting of the duality of opening and closing its eyes—is held within your belly. 222.
O Śivā, you who are the Supreme beyond all afflictions, the Great One, and the Absolute;
and since you are the mass of consciousness, that bliss which transcends the festivals of the senses then shines forth.
O Śivā, if you dissolve without parts into the state of universal withdrawal which is devoid of dissolution,
then you are Kālī of creation, by whom the universe, once cast out into the external realm, O Mother, is swiftly reclaimed.

O Auspicious Mother, you who stand upon the wheel of wind brought together by two opposing winds that have attained equilibrium, you remain established and swallow that which stays within the interval devoid of coming and going. 225.

O Goddess, that flame which has emerged from the fire within the crest-lock, piercing through the wheel of light (dhāmacakra) in succession and kindled by the drinking of the nectar of the upward-flowing moon— that too I perceive, O Goddess, while standing outside.
Within which, like the essence of a peacock’s egg, there is a variegated seat starting from the word;
that is the fivefold meaning, while you are the Unstruck Sound (Unmanī), the devourer of the preliminary words of the junctures.

O Śivā, you who have entered the very being of the entire universe, you are infinite, eternally manifest, and possess a form whose closing is the withdrawal of all existence; for, being unobstructed, you bring about the dissolution of that which has been withdrawn.
O Śivā, you are the thirteen rays of the eyes established by yourself in playful sport;
you consist of the fivefold meaning, you are the knower, and you are intoxicated by the subdued camphor.
O Śivā, these [energies] consume everything through the rays of power born of the senses along with the Mothers;
and you, O Supreme One, who delights in the Great Abode of remembrance, withdraw the universal form.
The face of Kālapālaka, the ender of Śiva, is like a drop of water fallen into the ocean of the universe;
therein, you—whose light is consciousness and who devours all—bear fullness, for here you are Sādhyakālī.
O Mother, that Yama— who, characterized by our mental constructs in the form of doubt, thinks "this is real" or "this is not"—
is indeed driven away by you, you who are skilled in the sport of restraining all beings.

O Mother, you are terrifying in the form of Yama within the heart of one who, while engaged in his duties, has become averse to the great festival of the state of perfect consciousness, having been crushed by his own fear.

That intoxicating conceit of "mine" directed toward wealth, wife, face, and objects of enjoyment, as well as that egoism which resides in what is not the self—both of these are your seat in the form of death. (234)

O Mother, with unimpeded compassion, you bring about the corpse-like seat for the three worlds deluded by time—their internal exertion consisting of the fluctuations of consciousness—by pouring forth death. 235.

O Mother, by means of the flame of consciousness—which radiates eternally and illumines the entire path of the senses—this world, consisting of the fivefold objects of experience, has been rendered auspicious within your inner being. 236.
O Śivā, you who consist of latent impressions (vāsanā) and are the abode of worldly existence, having brought about the dissolution of the universe,
Bhava— along with his latent impressions— was indeed withdrawn in an instant by your curved eyebrow.

O Mother, tell me: when that power (kalā) of yours, which creates the diversity of the universe and wanders within the circle of the knowable, turns toward you—then, by means of your crooked creative activity (kriyā), she becomes yours. 238.
O Mother, from the midst of the ultimate reality, by means of Your infinite form— which possesses the solar orb that both opens and closes its eyes—
the form of fire is created by You here, and it is also consumed by You at the single dawn.

O Mother, this crest-flame of Bhāravi, named Bharga, which was directed toward the fuel of the objects of the senses, indeed finds its extinction in you, the sole fire of Śiva, who abides in the abode of peace. 240.

That Sun of Consciousness, who causes the fivefold objects—which resemble an egg of nectar—to manifest for living beings, withdraws half of them within and emits that same fivefold object-world externally. (241)
O Mother, you whose limit is known as the upward-sounding resonance of the gathered [elements], whose body is clearly adorned and radiant—
you indeed abide as the devourer of the essence of the universe for the sake of illuminating the digit characterized by Time.
Eager to drink the honey of various objects contained within the jar of the wheel of existence,
that which was the domain of the sun’s rays now perishes like a moth in your radiance.
This vital breath (prāṇa) is called the time of Yama; it is the fire within the central channel, O Mother.
Having led this Rudra upward to the supreme void, you shall render him averse to further creation there.
This is that very wrath, fierce as the fire of cosmic dissolution, which has eclipsed the orb of the sun with your foot;
its rays, possessing terrifying power and a relish for devouring the universe, have been quelled by you.

O Giver of Boons, because they seize what is to be grasped before them as something separate, those rays even carry away the life-force from that [grasping]; yet, having surrendered the expansion of the world to You, they are truly the perceivers.

O Mother, you who swallow even the renowned Mahākāla— difficult to seize like a fire that consumes the oblation— you devour that seeker who takes pleasure here in this cremation ground named Karavīra, which is a voracious eater of living beings.
The *Dikcarī* (the Sky-walker of the Directions) manifests externally in the ten directions through those respective sense organs;
and the *Antarcarī* (the Inner Sky-walker) and the *Khecarī* (the Space-walker), O Mother, manifest within the three internal instruments—these are dear to You. 248.

O Mother! Since the creation of Tvaṣṭṛ, the sun of auspicious awakening, those rays which ascend through the three steps of the twelve-fold sequence—in them you move, or perhaps you are the thirteenth. (249)
Through the state of being mixed with both sequential and non-sequential [orders], Your sequence is a beautiful vision of the triad;
You are the sole ground of the power of the qualities of the fourth ray, and You are Kālī, formidable through the three qualities of the sequence.

O Kālī, since ten of your hands are stationed there and two others rise from that place, you resort to that sky which is supreme on all sides; for you are the auspicious moonlight of the light of Śiva.
O Mother, you are that which is peaceful and undifferentiated from the sky, and that which, though a mass of light, is itself set aside;
you are that which shines beyond both dualistic states, wherein you dissolve as the multitude of liberated ones.

O Śivā, you, having embraced Śaṅkara— who is free from all negation and whose arising is pregnant with the three states— emit from every side the Nāda, which shines with a single flavor and possesses an imperishable expansion.

To those who know Your form to be such as this, and to those who have constantly made the effort to be absorbed in it, You are composed of nectar; but to those who perceive otherwise, You are composed of poison.
He who causes the deluded mind to be purified also delivers the wise;
for by him, that ocean of the nectar of existence is led to a state of wavelessness for those who enjoy it in Śiva. 255.

O Umā, that body of yours is the abode of the Goddess of Consciousness, which you bear as a lotus in the ocean of the nectar of existence— a sea filled with the ambrosia of the five objects of sense and overflowing with the raft of bliss.
There, O Mother, the person— having entered into dissolution within the delicious maṇḍala of the lotus-light altar—
is closed by illusion (māyā), yet, enveloped by knowledge (vidyā), he opens his eyes.

O Mother, where the lotus of consciousness—resplendent with the petals of its respective objects, blossoming and radiant, and overflowing with the nectar of your contemplative awareness—attains the state of a pedestal. 258.
O Śivā, you who dissolve the three impurities, you have taken refuge in the Pūrṇapīṭha which is identical with the Great Self;
you are the embodiment of the pure sun, the flow of the essence of bliss consisting of the manifestation of non-duality for the virtuous.

O Śivā, you who possess a smiling countenance rest upon a lotus—the seat of the sixteen-fold inner essence (kalā) of the womb, which is filled with the nectar of the six oceans and whose petals are the various arts (kalās)—a lotus that has abandoned the cycle of coming and going for the sake of the deceased. 260.

O Caṇḍikā, if the body of the moon—stainless, showing no sign of waning, swelling like cotton through night and day, and wherein consciousness and insentience are submerged in its own self-luminosity—is indeed equal [to You], [then let it be so]. 261.
But those who abide in the lineage of Kuṇḍalī and Śikhā, and those who possess the *akula-bindu*,
O Mother— they indeed know Your majesty, which consumes the universe that consists of the light of plenitude.
O Mother! By Your flame of light, the haughty darkness within the mind of man is dispelled;
You who are marked by the sign of the expansion of that path are indeed Śiva and Śakti themselves. (263)

O Mother, you bear a radiant body that conceals the rays of hundreds of suns rising [simultaneously] and the moonlight from hundreds of moons whose spots are hidden; having caused me to enter that very essence, make me free from all ailment. 264.
O Mistress whose nature is the shining senses, you who are the moon, sun, and fire for the lineage;
remembered now within the pavilion of the sages' minds, grant me refuge at your feet. 265.
O Caṇḍikā, grasping the entire sphere of objects with your faces— which possess the characteristics of the fivefold power— you cast them into me and thus perform your innate sacrifice.

O Śivā, here in this world the circle of perfected ones (siddhacakra) rejoices, their impurities shaken off by the remembrance of your feet and their full splendor radiating everywhere; alas, even the full moon does not remove my torment.
The body, which devours time and contains within it the objects of the past, future, and present, is worshipped as Kālakarṣiṇī;
yogis carry her from the form of Kṛṣṇa onwards through her universal manifestation.
Arising from touch, form, taste, smell, and sound, it shatters the nature of consciousness through its power;
it is the activity that traverses the six paths formed by succession, as well as the wheel of forms consisting of space and time.

O Ambikā, that state which is luminous, dark, and non-coloring—its very essence here, being existent, is the Kula characterized by the moon, fire, and sun; and you, though abiding in the fourth state, are its imperceptible beauty.

O Mother, O Auspicious One, he who possesses exalted majesty rejoices everywhere through the sight of you; and you, who are honored by the eyes of all, carry with your wisdom the sovereignty over the entire world.
O Kālī! Having beheld [Thee] with extraordinary divine eyes, Thy majesty is described;
yet, O Umā, even this mere description is but the chatter of a servant for Thy delight. 272.
O Mother, you are neither male nor female, for you are the very nature of consciousness; yet you possess no neuter state either.
Nor do you possess the threefold form of the husband; without you, even that triad would not manifest.
O Mother, the Lord is some inconceivable being, beginningless and endless, possessed of a great mind;
you are his manifestation, the devourer of the universe. Therefore, who here is capable of dividing you?
You are the divider of the red and white-bodied swans, and your husband possesses a form fashioned by you;
through the distinction between the rays of the sun and the moon, you are yourself both some woman and a man.
O Mother, your radiant form appears before us as divided into five colors;
yet even when mixed with you, it remains unstable and is thus designated as "variegated" (citra), being of four kinds.
Furthermore, O Jyotir-añjana, presided over by the power that obscures manifestation, you are twofold:
known as Vigraha, Ābharaṇa, Bindu, and Śarvarī; you are the source of emergence, the origin of existence, and manifestly arisen.
When mixed with collyrium, your complexion shines red when the mixture is equal;
when the collyrium is in excess, your body becomes dark blue, and when your luster is in excess, it becomes yellowish-white. (278)

O Mother, when your body is mild due to the desire to create, and likewise fierce when there is a desire to protect, yet this very fierceness turns into peacefulness when you remember your own abode with the intent to withdraw [the world]. (279)
In your radiant, all-pervading body, the multitude of distinct worlds clearly submerges,
just as they shine within the cage of light when Śiva presides over the fire of time.
O Mother, that form of yours which is devoid of the threefold form, yet pregnant with the threefold form,
consisting of consciousness and characterized by the supreme form, shines both within and without.

" 'Woman' is merely some conceptual construction belonging to you; even the form of womanhood is such a mental construct. In reality, you are the universal embodiment, the supreme consciousness of Śiva herself. (282)
O Śivā, you abide in the fourth state, yet you are established in that which is the second;
O Śivā, he who relies upon the fifth state is also established in that which is the third. (283)
That state which is first, that which follows it, and the one beyond that—into those you enter as she who goes to the Fourth (Turyā).
You are the body of the Fourth, having drawn in the Triad; you enter the Fifth, having fulfilled the Triad.

O Ambareśvarī, although you are formless, everything is manifested through your possession of all forms; for you, who abide upon the seat of the expansion of non-dual bliss-consciousness, shine forth eternally. (285)

Neither the Vedas, nor words, nor the scriptures—whose intentions are fixed upon fragmented objects—lead you, O Supreme Goddess; nor do sacrifices, rituals, or the rules of yoga lead you to such a state.

O Mother, even the conceptualization of the path of knowledge and yoga directed toward that state characterized by qualities such as eternity does not grant the experience of You, unless one takes refuge in Your dissolution alone as the sole Guru. (287)

O Mother, those whose minds are fixed on the state of the void and who, having perceived the world through intuition, are censured— you enter into them incessantly, for they are beheld by you with your profound guidance.
O beautiful one, those qualities of yours— eternality, omnipresence, fullness, and the innate range of vision and action—
as well as passion, knowledge, and all the arts, shine forth like various ornaments upon the sky.

O Mother! The host of deities, who are non-dual and whose unity is established within the expanse of the sky, shine forth even in the sphere of Your exertion; though all-pervading, they become the locus of immediate dissolution even without You.

Thus, O Mother, the arising of your fivefold function—a marvel of diverse manifestations—shines forth at all times and in every direction, possessing its own innate nature which is entirely unfragmented. (291)

For you indeed are the birthplace of the gods for that one in whom the sequenceless order of deities— consisting of the twenty-five elements, which are the support for all things other than the fragmented [limited] womb— arises incessantly.

Abiding within the expanse of the power of divine speech, the source from which the circle of rays emerges, your imperishable process of withdrawal arises unconstructed within your nine-syllabled form. (293)

O Gaurī! You are the one whose innate state arises from the beginning of the voidness of the object of perception; you do not differ from your own supreme peak which is full of its inception; you possess a body that is a wheel of rays yet are devoid of rays; and you are the latent impression of excellent merit. (294)

O Kālī, you are the unobstructed seat of mantra—the supreme, non-dual foundation whose seed-syllable is the lotus, which is the abode of no fixed dwelling, the sequence for blending with the path of sound, and which, though one in conception, possesses manifold divisions. 295.

O Mother, though you are the fullness of vibration, you have become free from vibration, unobstructed, of the nature of space, and the locus for all sequential processes— the Pīṭha [of consciousness] together with Ambā, the Vidyā that transcends all limits.

O Goddess worshipped by the hosts of Rudras, Siddhas, and sages! You are the Person (Puruṣa) whose lotus-petals are the eight sources of birth, while you are the casket of the powers residing within the petals; you are the Lord, and your form is the Liṅga.

O Mother! Grant me that celebrated ninefold wheel of yours, which consists of the fourfold group originating from the beginning of creation, which arises from the multitude of forms resembling light, and which occupies the fragmented seats within the sacred pīṭhas.
O Goddess, you are the embodiment of the nine-syllable mantra and the inner wheel; you have placed all the deities within your own belly.
Pervaded by the seventeen syllables, O Goddess, you move toward Śiva, the moon of illumination. 299.

The lineage of gurus, beginning with Śiva and ending with Somapa, which takes delight solely in your transmission—this entire sequence from Cakrabhānu down to Ānanāgra has been attained by you through this [teaching]. (300)

O Śivā, that which is my own nature—characterized by non-dual awareness (advaya-vimarśa), devoid of succession, yet possessing a divine form manifested through consciousness, maintaining the sequence of various objects and persons—is Your supreme state. 301.
Following that, the subtle characteristic, consisting of light and devoid of color, is intended;
having first described this gross [form], it is observed and meditated upon by me in order to pacify the mind. (302)

In that auspicious state, O Śāntavatī, you have realized—like the sky—that which is beyond sensation within the human impurity; thus, through the expansion of the rays of consciousness, you have achieved the unimpeded performance of all tasks.
O Mother, having set aside the Son of Soma, this sequence of yours centered upon me has today been praised by me in some measure;
for this terrifying cycle of existence has been swallowed up by the splendor of the contemplation of your lotus feet.

I have indeed been released by you; I have been impelled by that tongue of yours which is worthy of me, to [compose] a commentary on the hymn to Your feet composed by Siddhanātha, and the *pañcikā* (fivefold exposition) composed by Kālidāsa. (305)
O Mother, whoever knows that hymn of yours which consists of words of definitive certainty, let him make the world his mouth;
for, having taken refuge at your feet like Kālidāsa, my speech has blossomed through your grace.
May the world, whose mind is deluded today, be liberated by those very qualities of yours;
having understood you as the full pedestal (pīṭha), this auspicious hymn has been composed by me for the sake of your grace. || 307 ||
O Goddess! Has this hymn of praise to the Moonlight of the Consciousness-Sky produced any desired fruit for me?
For whoever recites or chants this hymn to You, whoever explains its meaning here, and whoever understands it—[for them, all desires are fulfilled]. (308)
O Goddess, grant success to him who, having followed [the path], enacts his desired [aim];
[grant it] for this hymn of praise to You composed here with one hundred and nine verses, O showerer of timely rain.
Daily grasping the wheel of time with *triṣṭubh* meters and transcending it, he becomes serene;
that which you have discerned after reflection—that Śiva desires the welfare of men—is now known. 310.
O Gaurī, you who are praised by those whose intellects are swift, bestow all that is desired upon Viśvarājñī;
yet my sole desire, O Śivā, is your glance toward me from every side.
By which Śiva constantly enters me, that ocean of the flowing and swelling of saliva. || 311 ||
Out of reverence for that state of being, Śrīvatsa composed this hymn of praise for the sake of attaining perfection at Pūrṇapīṭha; indeed, O Great Secret, he performed it for the benefit of men.
Thus ends the *Cidgaganacandrikā*, composed by the great poet Śrī Kālīdāsa.
The verses of praise accompanied by the *Kramaprakāśikā*:
In this Tantra, he is the foremost in destroying ignorance with the rays of his awakening, like the sun.

I bow to that wise Gopīnātha, the light of Sarasvatī, who shines brilliantly with the splendor of the world-illuminating moon-lotus cluster, and in whose heart the waves of the ocean of the nectar of eternal peace perpetually sway. || 1 ||
Mīmāṃsā, white as nectar, suddenly bestows upon them the treasure of the power of awakening to the immortal truth of Vedānta, like Brahmā, the mine of knowledge;
and in their hearts, the unfathomable ocean of logic sports with its restless, dancing waves.
We ever praise those lords of Badarī, who are the future manifestations of the glory of the one named Śukla. || 2 ||

I consider the venerable scholar Śrī Raghunāthaśarman to be a stainless teacher of knowledge and a guide upon the path, in whom the Vedāṅgas shine like gems with their ancillaries in the ocean of jewels;
for by his praise, the creeper of his fame shines throughout the world like nectar, and he himself appears as an immortal god.
I constantly remember that worshipful Śaṅkara, the bestower of happiness and the source of knowledge.

Now, in this white abode of learning, the wise and excellent Vrajavallabha shines forth as a renowned master of yoga and the weight of the Tantras, distinguished by his division of the lotuses [of the heart];
in my mind, no other cause for his excellence appears but his boundless compassion.
I meditate upon that inspirer, who is ever-new and who assists me in the work of commentary. || 4 ||
My father, a proud worshiper of Śrī Śiva, and my mother, Ramā, who bestows delight— having now obtained at their side a powerful family of mental strength,
I have composed this new commentary on the *Cidgaganacandrikā*, which possesses fresh vigor and is supreme for illuminating the meaning.
I entreat the compassionate ones, who possess wisdom and are filled with an intellect adorned by learning, that they grant me the awakening of understanding.
Having obtained as my helper the one whose hand is clasped by the illustrious Rukmiṇī, I am here in this world without obstacle in the region renowned as Sīvāna.
My dwelling is on the beautiful ground along the Sarayū river.
In that tradition, the venerable Raghunātha Miśra exerted great effort; his commentary, the *Vimalā*, which illuminates the meaning, is found in the *Vibhāgatantra*.
He composed that [work] titled *Arthaprakāśikā*.
What is the fifth? It is that which, by assisting in the establishment of the fruitfulness of the *Arthaprakāśikā*, serves to destroy doubt; it is the one with the face of a serpent (*nāgānanā*).
She is the destroyer of delusion and the bearer of the burden of the wise.
The sun, the illuminator of the world and its beyond, always shatters the petals of dense darkness;
the mass of flames intensely rends the fear of those who tremble;
and the lofty wind-borne showers burn away the vast waves of heat.
O Mother, your single glance alone pacifies everything here.
One should maintain an auspicious family lineage.
